sources.quote: Dear Galton, Your Tacitus is a charming little book, and your preface, like everything you write, very perfect in its sanity of wise criticism and good English. Many thanks for your gift. I still hope that Tiberius was very wicked, but fear that philology was his only crime. Ever yours
sources.context: Wilde to Arthur Galton, [October 1890], 16 Tite Street (MS Montague) - quoted whole. The book is the Camelot Classics Tacitus of October 1890. THE SAME YEAR Galton received Lionel Johnson's letter about Wilde.
sources.speaker: Oscar Wilde
sources.supports: The whole of the correspondence, and that the two men were in contact in 1890.
sources.provenance: Repo PDF page 477; printed folio 455 confirmed on the rendered page image, read 2026-08-06.

name: Arthur Galton
bio: Writer and editor (1852-1921), who edited a translation of the Tacitus Annals published in the Camelot Classics in 1890. One letter from Wilde survives, thanking him for it.
bio_note: Added 2026-08-06, clearing a backlog. NO CONNECTION LINE: one short letter about a book, and nothing states or implies more. HE IS ON THE MAP FOR A REASON EXTERNAL TO HIS OWN CORRESPONDENCE: he is the friend to whom [[lionel-johnson]] wrote, two days after first meeting Wilde in February 1890, 'I am in love with him' - the sentence that carries the `lionel-johnson--wilde` edge. The confidant of that declaration turns out to be a Wilde correspondent himself, in the same year, and the map was showing the declaration without showing who received it. ONE LETTER at printed 455, read at the page (2026-08-06). DATES 1852-1921 from the editors' note there.
